text: A prayer of David. Turn your ear, LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.
Guard my life, for I am devoted to you; save your servant who trusts in you—you are my God.

versions.text: Guard my life, for I am faithful to you; save your servant who trusts in you. You are my God.
versions.explanation: Hebrew 'chasid' describes one who is godly/devoted; 'faithful to you' supplies an object not in the Hebrew and can sound like a claim of merit. 'Devoted to you' keeps the covenant-loyalty sense. Joining the final clause with a dash also keeps the flow closer to the Hebrew, where 'you are my God' stands inside the appeal rather than as a separate sentence.

text: Be gracious to me, Lord, for I call to you all day long.
Bring joy to your servant's soul, for to you, Lord, I lift up my soul.
You, Lord, are good and forgiving, rich in mercy to all who call on you.
Hear my prayer, LORD; listen to the voice of my pleading.

versions.text: Hear my prayer, LORD; listen to my cry for mercy.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has 'the voice of my supplications' (plural), and the parallel imperatives are both about attentive listening. Rendering 'the voice of my pleading' preserves the fuller image and reads well aloud.

text: In the day of my distress I call on you, for you will answer me.
Among the gods there is none like you, Lord, and no deeds compare with yours.
All the nations you have made will come and bow before you, Lord, and give glory to your name.
For you are great and do wondrous things; you alone are God.
Teach me your way, LORD, that I may walk in your truth; give me an undivided heart, that I may fear your name.
I will praise you, Lord my God, with all my heart, and glorify your name forever.
For great is your steadfast love toward me; you have delivered my soul from the depths of Sheol.

versions.text: For great is your mercy toward me; you have delivered my soul from the depths of the grave.
versions.explanation: Two small gains: 'steadfast love' better matches 'chesed' and harmonizes with verse 15 ('abounding in love'), where the same word is used; and 'Sheol' (the realm of the dead) is more precise than 'the grave,' which suggests only a burial place. A brief footnote explaining Sheol as the place of the dead would help hearers.

text: O God, the arrogant have risen against me; a band of ruthless men seeks my life, and they give no thought to you.
But you, Lord, are a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in love and faithfulness.
Turn to me and have mercy on me; grant your strength to your servant and save the son of your handmaid.
Give me a sign of your goodness, so that those who hate me may see it and be put to shame, for you, LORD, have helped me and comforted me.
